Subject: POC/trial planning: workload profile & success criteria (AcmeHealth)

Hi Liam
Great to speak earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC (trial) scoped and scheduled. I copied Ben (solutions) so he can own setup and traffic routing.

Summary of what we discussed:
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference for AcmeHealth's clinical QA assistant for intake notes.
- Key success criteria (proposed):
  * Performance: p95 response latency < 200ms for typical queries; p95 < 350ms for long-context queries.
  * Reliability: error rate < 0.1% during test window.
  * Throughput: support sustained 150 RPS with ability to handle spikes up to 400 RPS for short bursts.
  * Quality: >= 90% accuracy on a 50-sample evaluation set (we'll define metric/test set together).
  * Security/compliance: deployment within US regions, SOC 2 evidence shared, and HIPAA handling clarified.

Workload intake we need from you (attached template):
- Average and peak RPS (per endpoint)
- Typical prompt token length and completion length (median, 95th)
- Concurrency (active sessions) and session affinity requirements
- Burst patterns (duration & frequency of spikes) and acceptable degradation modes
- % of calls requiring streaming vs single-response
- Any data residency or encryption/KMS constraints

Proposed evaluation plan and timeline:
- Week of Apr 12: Trial provisioning + kickoff (2 weeks of traffic testing)
- Apr 12-Apr 23: Baseline testing + performance/load validation (we'll run predefined scenarios)
- Apr 26-Apr 30: Quality evaluation on agreed query set + decision/next steps

Ownership:
- Redwood: Ben (solutions) to provision endpoints and run load tests; Marissa to coordinate success criteria and procurement.
- AcmeHealth: Liam to provide workload profile, Sophie (security) for compliance docs, and a technical contact for data/sample access.

Next steps (action items):
1) Liam: fill the attached workload-profile-template.xlsx and send back (including any past traffic CSVs).
2) Marissa/Ben: prepare SOW template and trial config; share Drive folder and DocuSign link.
3) Schedule a 30-min kickoff for week of Apr 12 - propose Apr 12 at 10am PT unless you prefer another slot.

Attachments: workload-profile-template.xlsx, redwood-poc-sow-template.pdf

If that all looks good I'll schedule kickoff and Ben will start capacity planning based on what you send.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa
Thanks for the clear write-up. Agree with the proposed success criteria; a few details from our side below and attached is a short CSV (acme_workload_summary_q1_2027.csv) with historical traffic.

Workload summary (per our analytics):
- Average RPS (global): ~20 RPS (during business hours)
- Typical sustained peak: ~180 RPS (last quarter during morning surge)
- Burst behavior: short bursts up to 400 RPS lasting ~30-90s, occurring ~3-5 times/day during outages/reloads
- Prompt tokens: median 120 tokens; 95th percentile 520 tokens (we have some long context cases)
- Completion tokens: median 40 tokens; 95th percentile 160 tokens
- Concurrency: typically 50-80 concurrent sessions, with spikes to ~200 when many agents run bulk backfills
- Streaming: ~30% of calls expect streaming for partial answers in the UI
- Security: HIPAA-covered workload; data must remain in US region, and we require KMS-based key control for any persisted artifacts. Sophie will own security questionnaire.

We also have a small batch of sample queries (anonymized) we can share once the NDA/SOW is in place.

On timing - Apr 12 kickoff works for us. Sophie, I'm looping you in to confirm security POC scope.

Thanks Liam
this is perfect and very helpful. A few clarifications and proposed test plan so Ben can size the trial environment correctly.

Clarifications:
- For the 95th token lengths (~520 prompt tokens) we'll provision for longer context models and run a subset of long-context tests separately to isolate latency impact.
- For bursts up to 400 RPS: can you confirm whether bursts are uniformly distributed across endpoints or concentrated on a single API route? That will affect auto-scaling setup.

Proposed technical test plan:
1) Provision a dedicated trial cluster in US-west with pinned model variant (open LLM x-small-quant) and a fallback to a cheaper variant on sustained overload.
2) Run baseline single-client latency tests (median/95th) for small (120/40) and long (520/160) token scenarios.
3) Run load tests to simulate:
   - Sustained 150 RPS over 15 minutes
   - Burst profile simulations: ramp to 400 RPS for 60s, repeated 4x with 10m intervals
   - Concurrency tests: 200 concurrent sessions over 10 minutes
4) Measure: latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token cost, and model quality on the held-out 50-sample set.

Proposed success thresholds (confirmable):
- p95 latency < 200ms for typical (120/40) use case; < 350ms for long context tests
- Error rate < 0.1%
- Quality >= 90% on agreed eval set

Procurement note: I'll send SOW/DSR for signature this week. Ben - can you start capacity planning and post initial sizing here?

If Liam/Sophie confirm bursts are across one route vs many, we'll adjust auto-scale policies accordingly.

Thanks,
Marissa
